scientific_scope_status: In the ideal equal-load one-scission interface with nu effective paths per area, peak traction=nu*f and scission work/area=nu*U_b, so their ratio is U_b/f. Required traction alone supplies no general fracture-work bound. Ideal constant-traction pullout gives work/area=sigma*ell and pays aligned fibre packing/material plus consumed sliding inventory. If each repair adds a seam that remains in series, n repairs create n(n+1)/2 independent seam-interval exposures. For periodic deep resets, n,k are positive integers,1<=k<=n, q=ceil(n/k), m_j=k for j<q and m_q=n-k*(q-1). With E=sum_{j=1}^q m_j*(m_j+1)/2, survival=(1-h)^E*(1-s)^q pays every actual deep connection, including the first, and requires complete unloading of old seams. Arbitrary partitions with blocks at most k are excluded. A constant-damage/first-order-recovery map gives a separate steady post-load active fraction; slow biological matter replacement does not acquire that fast recovery rate.
